ideas.one_liner: A continuous agent-readiness test suite for companies whose products are now used by AI agents: it runs real agents against your API, docs, SDK and checkout flows, scores whether they can finish the top jobs your customers care about, and shows exactly which step broke and what to change.

For platform/AI engineering teams running customer-facing agents that write to real systems (payments, CRM, email, bookings), Ledger is a thin proxy + console that records every write action with an idempotency fingerprint, detects when an action's outcome is uncertain or duplicated, and gives on-call a one-click "verify / reverse / confirm" workflow with a per-customer audit trail.

For engineering teams running production AI agents that touch money, tickets and customer comms, Doublecheck is a thin proxy + console that records every external write an agent attempts, resolves "did this actually commit?" when a tool call times out, and blocks duplicate payments, emails and refunds on retry or fork.

For the platform/AI-engineering team that owns production agents, Driftwatch watches the vendor surfaces those agents depend on — MCP tool schemas, model IDs, API docs and changelogs — and turns each change into a ranked "this will break these 3 agent flows, here's the diff and the fix PR" alert instead of a wall of release notes.

HoldLine is an AI caller for B2B back offices outside healthcare — the buyers, AR clerks and ops coordinators who burn hours on hold with carriers, suppliers, utilities, banks and government offices — that sits through the IVR and hold queue, asks a scripted set of questions, and returns a verified, structured answer card (plus transcript and recording) written straight back into the ERP/spreadsheet row.

Paste a GitHub skill repo or an `npx skills add owner/repo` command and get a one-screen, plain-English card per skill: what it tells your agent to do, which files/commands/network calls it touches, and the exact lines that look like prompt injection — before you install it.

For the platform or AppSec owner at a 200-2,000 person engineering org, SkillProof is the approval layer for agent skills: it discovers every SKILL.md installed across developer machines and repos, diffs each new version, and gives one person a 30-second approve/deny with the capability changes spelled out.
Upload a photo of any object — a espresso machine, a drone, a sneaker — and get back a labelled, exploded technical diagram you can edit part-by-part and export as SVG or PNG.

For the 2-10 person team shipping a production agent on the Cursor Agent SDK (or a similar Markdown-prompt + TypeScript-tools setup), EvalSeed reads the agent's repo and generates the first 50 eval cases — inputs, expected tool calls and graders — so the eval suite exists before the first incident instead of after.

For the AP manager or financial controller at a 50-500 person company with 200-2,000 suppliers in NetSuite, Xero or QuickBooks, Stalecheck re-verifies every supplier record against live public evidence each month — still trading, name/registration changed, insolvency filed, website dead, duplicate of another vendor — and hands back a ranked worklist of the 20 records that actually need a human.

Paste any list — your SaaS subscriptions, a 'top 50 AI tools' blog post, your CRM accounts, your bookmarks — and Deadlist tells you which of them are dead, acquired, renamed or pivoted, each with a citation and a date.

Paste a GitHub skills repo (or drop your .claude/skills folder) and Skillscale weighs every SKILL.md in tokens, shows what share of your agent's context window it eats before you type a word, and gives you a shareable "context weigh-in" card plus a public weekly leaderboard of the fattest skills in the ecosystem.

For the permit coordinator / job captain at a 5-50 person architecture, engineering or multi-site-rollout team, Backcheck turns a city's plan-check correction letter PDF into a complete, agency-formatted resubmittal package — every comment parsed and numbered, routed to the right discipline owner, a drafted code-cited response linked to the revised sheet, and a backcheck that refuses to export until every comment is closed.

Drop one ugly page — an invoice, a lab table, a scanned form — and Parsedoff shows you two anonymous parses of it side by side, you vote for the better one, then it reveals which model won and scores both against the new Document Parsing Protocol rules.

For the retail operations manager at a $5M-$100M CPG brand (and the 3PL account manager who ships for them), Dockproof turns each retailer's routing guide plus the brand's own chargeback history into a per-PO pre-ship checklist that must be cleared before the truck leaves — and files the cleared checklist, label scans and photos as a dated evidence packet that wins the dispute if a deduction lands anyway.

For the creative/influencer ops lead at a DTC brand or UGC-ads agency, Rightsline connects to the brand's own Meta and TikTok ad accounts, matches every live creator ad to its licence and platform authorization code, and raises one alert before an ad either loses its rights or stops delivering — with a one-click pause or renewal request.

Paste three paragraphs you actually wrote and Voiceprint shows four top models rewriting one of them, scores how much of your voice each one destroyed, hands you a copy-paste voice.md that stops it, and posts the week's model-vs-voice leaderboard.
